subject: Operator tenancy & software residency — redline coordination for on-prem addendum
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixsys.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helixsys.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator tenancy & software residency — redline coordination for on-prem addendum

Sara / Tom — thanks again for the productive call this morning. As discussed, Helix's procurement redlines introduced two clusters of material concern on our side: 1) the scope of operator tenancy (who may run support/maintenance processes inside the customer environment), and 2) software residency / data locality language tied to snapshots and forensic access.

I'm attaching a short draft "Residency Exhibit" and a redline of the MSA + Order Form that call out a couple of operational constraints we need Helix to accept for a private deployment:
- Limited operator tenancy: scoped to named Redwood employees for emergency troubleshooting, with time-boxed, auditable sessions.
- Witnessless snapshot deposit: instead of onsite witnessing, we propose a signed digest + time-stamped snapshot pushed to an agreed object store under joint-control metadata.
- Jurisdictional residency: runtime and backups must remain within the nominated AWS region; cross-region failover requires written approval.

Can you confirm whether Helix can accept the residency exhibit approach in principle? If so, we'll circulate a tighter redline that converts the high-level asks into contract language (exhibits and Order Form exhibits).

Attachments: [Helix_MSAA-OrderForm_redline.docx (docx)], [Residency_Exhibit_v1_draft.docx (docx)]

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Counsel, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0187

--
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixsys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helixsys.com>, procurement@helixsys.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator tenancy & software residency — redline coordination for on-prem addendum

Hi Soojin — thanks for the summary and the materials. We reviewed the proposal with Helix legal and infra. A few quick clarifications before we loop in our contracts team:

1) Witnessless snapshot deposit: we need details on the digest/signing mechanism. Does Redwood propose an HSM-signed digest or a PKI approach where Helix maintains a key? Who holds the snapshot encryption keys?

2) Operator tenancy: Helix's security policy prefers a named role model but also requires that any Redwood temporary access be logged to our SIEM and limited to jump-hosted bastion sessions. Is there any objection to specific SIEM forwarding/agent installation?

3) Jurisdictional residency: we will accept region-level residency for runtime only if backups are mirrored to a secondary region for DR; we need that option in the Order Form exhibit.

We'll schedule a short technical sync with Markus and David if that helps. For now, our contracts lead (cc: procurement) wants an editable exhibit with crisp acceptance criteria they can sign.

Regards,
Sara Jensen
Head of Cloud Operations, Helix Systems
sara.jensen@helixsys.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixsys.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator tenancy & software residency — redline coordination for on-prem addendum

Sara — appreciate the quick read. High-level legal position from our side: we can accommodate Helix's SIEM requirement and the named-role model, but we need reciprocal protections and operational controls baked into the exhibit and Order Form. Key items to incorporate in the next draft: 

- Defined "Operator Session" process: written request, limited to <2 hours unless extended by mutual email, mandatory session recording and hash delivered to Helix within 24 hours.
- For signing/digest: Redwood proposes signed digests using our KMS-backed signing key; we will provide key fingerprint and verification steps. If Helix insists on locally held keys, we need a separate key escrow and HSM attestation clause.
- Snapshot custody and encryption: snapshots will be encrypted with a customer-specific envelope key; Redwood will not retain plaintext. The exhibit must include acceptance criteria for proving snapshot integrity (signed manifests, hash chains).
- DR/backups: to meet Helix's secondary-region DR ask we can add an opt-in checkbox in the Order Form that triggers replicated backups with associated runbook obligations and RTO/RPO commitments.

I'll attach a marked PDF showing clause-level edits; the exhibit draft should be treated as the master for commercial acceptance. We prefer the signed-digest model (witnessless) to minimize onsite legal overhead, but we can accommodate witnessing for high-security customers as a priced add-on.

Attachment: [Operator-Tenancy-Appendix_marked.pdf (pdf)]

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@helixsys.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: david.kim@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator tenancy & software residency — redline coordination for on-prem addendum

Sara / Soojin — happy to jump on a quick tech sync. Operational notes from infra: 

- SIEM forwarding: we support forwarding via syslog/HTTPS; we will provide a hardened connector container that runs with minimal privileges. Installation by Helix infra team is preferred.
- Signed-digest workflow: our plan is to produce a tarball snapshot, compute a SHA-256 tree hash, then sign the manifest with Redwood's KMS. We can publish the signed manifest to the agreed S3 bucket (ACL: helix-protected) and push metadata to the joint Drive link.
- Key custody: default is Helix-owned envelope key (you provide the public material); Redwood holds an encrypted copy for rollback assistance only under the handback protocol (which requires two-party approval).
- Time windows: emergency operator sessions need to be limited and audited — we propose a 2-hour default session with a 30-minute pre-notify window for non-emergencies.

Technical sync suggestions: Wed 16 Jun 11:00 PT or Thu 17 Jun 09:00 PT.

Markus Klein
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator tenancy & software residency — redline coordination for on-prem addendum

Thanks all — good alignment. Next steps / mutual action plan: 

1) Redwood to produce Exhibit v1.1 with Laura's clause edits incorporated and a short technical appendix from Markus (due EOD Thu 17 Jun).
2) Helix to confirm preferred key custody model (Helix-led envelope key or HSM escrow) and whether SIEM agent installation is acceptable (response by Fri 18 Jun).
3) Technical sync scheduled: Wed 16 Jun 11:00 PT (Markus / David / Helix infra) — Markus to send invite.
4) Once Helix confirms, procurement/legal to exchange a redline of the Order Form; if Helix requires witness-based snapshot validation we will provide a priced exhibit.

I'll circulate the v1.1 exhibit and updated Order Form redline once Laura's edits are merged. If procurement needs a shorter commercial summary for exec sign-off, David can produce a one-page compliance snapshot.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Counsel, Redwood Inference
